evidence: M-O s.v. holy water, after Du Cange and Marco Polo (c. 1300)
terms.comment: Water blessed by a priest, from benedīcere. The West keeps it in a stoup by the church door for the sign of the cross; the East blesses water solemnly at Theophany, and the faithful drink it and sprinkle their houses with it.

evidence: Vulg. Num. 5.17: assūmetque aquam sānctam in vāse fictilī
terms.comment: The Vulgate’s phrase, of the holy water of the Law.
Lewis & Short translate Ovid’s phrase “holy water”; it is the water of pagan rites.

phrases.english: The priest is sprinkling the house with holy water.

sources: Lewis & Short: aqua · Lewis & Short: benedico · Lewis & Short: lustralis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. holy water.
